Marketing Executive
Department: Sales
Employment Type: Full Time
Location: Paris

Description
We’re seeking a Marketing Executive to propel our brand’s growth through impactful and innovative campaigns. In this role, you’ll oversee the creation of compelling content, fine-tune our digital marketing strategies, and use data insights to drive stronger customer engagement.
To thrive, you’ll need solid experience across SEO, SEM, and email marketing, along with excellent project management abilities and a collaborative, forward-thinking approach. If you’re passionate about finding fresh ways to connect with audiences and elevate a brand’s presence, we’d love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities
As a Marketing Executive, you’ll lead the planning and delivery of creative campaigns that strengthen our brand and support our growth goals. You’ll manage and produce engaging content across all digital channels, ensuring it aligns with our voice and values. You’ll develop, implement, and refine digital marketing strategies — with a strong focus on SEO, SEM, and email marketing — and use performance data to optimize engagement and reach. Working closely with internal teams and external partners, you’ll keep projects on track, juggle multiple priorities, and ensure everything meets the highest standards. Staying ahead of industry trends and bringing fresh, innovative ideas to the table will be key to your success in this role.

Skills, Knowledge and Experience
The ideal Marketing Executive will have strong expertise in digital marketing strategies, including SEO, SEM, and social media management. A creative mindset with a data-driven approach is essential, along with proficiency in content creation and campaign optimization. Experience using analytics tools, marketing automation platforms, and email marketing software is a plus. The ability to collaborate cross-functionally and manage multiple projects effectively is key to success in this role.

We are seeking a candidate with a diverse skill set to excel in a dynamic marketing environment. Below are the key skills we think are required to thrive in this role:

Essential

• Strong communication and copywriting skills

• Proficiency in digital marketing platforms (Google Ads, Facebook Ads, etc.)

• Data analysis and performance tracking (Google Analytics, etc.)

• Experience in campaign management and strategy development

• Proven ability to increase customer engagement and conversions

• Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field

Desirable

• Experience with SEO and content marketing

• Familiarity with marketing automation tools (HubSpot, Marketo, etc.)

• Knowledge of email marketing best practices

• Advanced degree or certifications in Marketing or a related discipline

About the Job

We are looking for a Salesforce Business Analyst to play a central role in our move from a legacy CRM to Salesforce. At IC, Salesforce is where our sales, retention, partner, compliance and support teams work every day, and the rules behind it are rich: who owns a client depends on their region, how they joined and whether they trade or introduce others, and what each team can see depends on role and regulated entity. You will be the bridge between those teams and our developers and QA, turning how the business really works into clear user stories, sound process and access designs, and an org people want to use. If you enjoy untangling complex processes, asking the question nobody has asked yet and seeing a requirement through to UAT, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll own

• Run workshops, interviews and process walkthroughs with Sales, Partners, Compliance and Support to understand how work is really done.

• Map current and future-state processes for the CRM migration, from sign-up through onboarding to trading, and identify gaps against the legacy system.

• Write clear user stories with acceptance criteria in Jira, plus BDD scenarios or specifications where a story needs more detail, traceable from business goal to delivered feature.

• Work with the Product Owner, Salesforce Architect, developers and QA to shape scalable solutions that follow Salesforce best practice.

• Contribute to defining data models, assignment rules and access requirements with the Salesforce technical team.

• Plan data migration with the technical team: field mapping, data quality rules and validation of migrated records.

• Maintain process documentation, data dictionaries, user guides and training materials, and drive user adoption after each release.

• Define and run test cases for system, integration and user acceptance testing, support production validation, and triage issues with QA and developers through to root cause.

• Use AI tools such as Claude to draft BRDs, stories and UAT scenarios and to surface edge cases, checking every output before it is used.

• Identify where automation or AI agents could remove manual work for sales and support teams.

• Define how success is measured, such as handling time, manual touches and conversion, and track it after release.

• Run demos and status updates, and communicate progress, risks and dependencies to management.

What you’ll need

Essential

• 5+ years as a Salesforce Business Analyst.

• Proven experience on a CRM migration or system transformation project.

• Strong knowledge of the Salesforce data model and core clouds, especially Sales and Service Cloud.

• Salesforce Administrator, Sales Cloud and Service Cloud Consultant certification.

• User stories, acceptance criteria and process flows that developers and testers can work from without guessing.

• A working understanding of Salesforce security: profiles, permission sets, roles and sharing.

• Experience in trading or financial services: client onboarding, partner management or compliance workflows.

• Agile/Scrum delivery with Jira.

• Effective prompting of AI tools such as Claude, including AI-assisted test case design for UAT.

Desirable

• A business analysis certification, such as Salesforce Certified Business Analyst, IIBA CBAP or CCBA, or PMI-PBA

• Data migration projects and large data sets, including Data Loader or similar tools

• Agentforce and AI-powered automation: defining agent use cases and taking them through UAT

• Brokerage or fintech experience: KYC/AML, trading account types, MT4, MT5 or cTrader, IB models

• Process modelling in tools such as Miro, Lucidchart or Visio

• Basic SQL or SOQL and Postman, to check data and API payloads yourself

• Multi-region, multi-language orgs

About the Job

We are looking for a Salesforce Developer who approaches Salesforce development through the lens of modern software engineering. At IC, Salesforce is where our sales, retention, partner and support teams work every day. We maintain a modular DX codebase, enforce clean object-oriented design patterns, build Lightning Web Components to a consistent design system, and follow strict code-quality and testing practices. If you enjoy writing clean, decoupled Apex, designing reactive and localised LWC frontends, and working in a modern Git and scratch-org workflow without legacy clutter, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll own

• Turn requirements into technical designs, then deliver Apex and Lightning Web Components for our support, sales, KYC, trading account, payment and partner workflows.

• Work with our trigger framework and Unit of Work, query builder, collection utilities, async actions and batch frameworks.

• Build reusable Lightning Web Components to our design system, with a custom label for every string and locale-aware formatting.

• Build and maintain REST integrations with payload validation, resilient error handling and mockable tests.

• Write bulkified, governor-aware code and async pipelines, and resolve performance bottlenecks and technical debt.

• Implement permission set groups, custom permissions, sharing and field-level security for every new feature.

• Write deterministic tests that check behaviour, not just coverage.

• Release through scratch orgs, pull requests and automated validation, from stage to UAT to production.

• Own features from design to production, delivering scalable, well-documented code to our engineering standards.

What you’ll need

Essential

• 3+ years of hands-on Salesforce development in an enterprise org.

• Strong Apex: triggers, Queueable, Batch and Scheduled jobs, bulkification and governor limits.

• Strong LWC and modern JavaScript (ES6+): lifecycle hooks, reactivity and component composition.

• Object-oriented design: SOLID principles and common design patterns.

• REST integrations: outbound callouts, inbound Apex REST, JSON, and Named and External Credentials.

• Solid SOQL skills: selective queries, indexing and safe dynamic query generation for large data volumes.

• Salesforce DX, sf CLI, Git, GitHub and a pull-request workflow.

• Salesforce Platform Developer I certification.

Your approach

• You read existing code before adding to it, and your changes look like they belong.

• You ask what problem a ticket solves before you estimate it, and flag gaps in a requirement early.

• You support your features after release and fix your own bugs first.

• You communicate clearly with developers, BAs and QA, including colleagues in other time zones.

• You’re keen to learn the trading domain: accounts, IBs, KYC and multi-entity regulation.

Desirable

• Salesforce Platform Developer II, or a Sales/Service Cloud Consultant certification

• Hands-on experience using Generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, or GitHub Copilot) for code generation, Apex/LWC refactoring, test class generation, and rapid debugging.

• Unlocked packages and package-based development

• Event-driven design with Platform Events

• Service Cloud experience, including CTI and call-centre integrations

• Brokerage or fintech experience: KYC/AML, MT4, MT5 or cTrader, IB models

• Coordinate interviews, follow up on feedback, maintain regular communication with candidates, and ensure timely progress throughout the recruitment process

• Provide administrative and operational support to the People Experience team, including onboarding coordination, HR projects, and other departmental activities as required

• Maintain professional communication and service standards with candidates, employees, and internal stakeholders, consistently upholding the company’s values of Ethics, Commitment, and Innovation

Required Skills & Experience

• 1+ years of experience in recruitment or a related role; FX industry experience is an advantage

• Degree in HR, Business Administration, or a related field; CIPD certification is an advantage

• Excellent written and verbal English

• Arabic is an advantage

• Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills

• High attention to detail and accuracy

• Proactive, resourceful, and quick to learn, with a continuous improvement mindset

• Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple vacancies and deadlines

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively

• Professional communication and interpersonal skills

• Good knowledge of recruitment platforms, social media, and Microsoft Office; ATS experience is an advantage

• Ability to work under pressure and adapt to changing priorities

Further Info:

• The role can be either in Limassol, Cyprus or Amman, Jordan or Dubai, UAE

• Working hours are 09:00 – 18:00 Monday to Friday or as per the departmental flextime arrangement

OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Hong Kong, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About The Opportunity

We are looking for a Product Manager with a deep understanding of TradingView users, strong commercial judgment, and experience driving product growth. You will grow OKX's business within the TradingView ecosystem by identifying the most promising customer segments, defining why traders should choose OKX, and finding effective ways to acquire, activate, and retain them, with accountability for measurable business outcomes.

Your first priority is to establish how the business can grow and which opportunities warrant investment. You will validate growth hypotheses through user research, data analysis, and focused experiments before committing substantial engineering resources. Those insights will shape the product roadmap, investment priorities, and the TradingView integrations and trading experience improvements you deliver with engineering and partners.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Define the Growth Strategy and Business Opportunity —

Identify high-potential customer segments, trading use cases, and market opportunities within the TradingView ecosystem. Assess competitive positioning, platform selection drivers, and OKX's differentiated value proposition. Build growth hypotheses and business cases that consider audience size, revenue potential, acquisition cost, and expected return, then set business goals, priorities, and a phased growth plan.

• Understand Users and the Trading Conversion Journey —

Use interviews, behavioral data, and community feedback to understand how traders discover platforms, use charts and indicators, set alerts, connect accounts, place orders, and manage positions. Identify what motivates or prevents users from choosing OKX, making their first trade, and returning. Develop customer segments and conversion funnels, and turn insights into clear product, positioning, and lifecycle opportunities.

• Validate Growth Hypotheses and Improve Conversion and Retention —

Design measurable experiments across acquisition, account connection, first successful trade, repeat trading, and reactivation. Use existing capabilities, onboarding, trader education, value proposition testing, and targeted campaigns to validate opportunities. Define success metrics, experiment costs, and criteria to scale or stop; expand approaches that work and use the evidence to inform subsequent product investment.

• Drive Go-To-Market and Ecosystem Partnerships —

Work with marketing, regional, lifecycle, and TradingView partner teams on acquisition and go-to-market plans. Evaluate ecosystem visibility, communities, creators, educational content, and joint campaigns as potential channels. Define the customer proposition, distribution approach, conversion journey, and partner objectives, and assess channels by the active traders, retention, and business contribution they generate.

• Translate Growth Evidence into Product Delivery and Integration —

Translate validated user needs and growth opportunities into a product roadmap, PRDs, and acceptance criteria. Define the minimum scope and engineering priorities required to achieve the business objective. Work with OKX engineering and TradingView technical teams to assess API integration, account authorization, market data, and order and position synchronization, and drive the necessary adaptation, testing, and launch to address specific conversion, trust, or retention problems.

• Own Business Outcomes and Continuously Refine Investment —

Own metrics for newly acquired trading users, first-trade conversion, active traders, retention, incremental trading volume, and revenue contribution, taking acquisition, incentive, and delivery costs into account. Separate the effects of market conditions, incentives, and product improvements. Review growth initiatives and feature investments, reallocate resources based on results, and track connection success and trading reliability as measures of experience quality.

What We Look For In You

•

Relevant product management experience in trading, fintech, or digital assets, with a track record of measurable product growth. You can explain how you identified opportunities, developed a growth strategy, and improved acquisition, trading conversion, retention, or revenue, including your personal contribution and results.

•

A deep understanding of TradingView users and their practical use of charts, indicators, watchlists, alerts, and trading workflows. You can explain why different traders choose a platform, switch terminals, abandon an order, or continue using a service, and validate those insights through research and data.

•

Strong commercial judgment and growth strategy skills. You can segment customers, assess opportunities, define differentiated positioning, select distribution channels, and build business cases. You validate demand and a credible path to growth through research and focused experiments before substantial engineering investment.

•

Strong analytical and experimentation skills. You can analyze funnels, cohorts, and retention, design and evaluate growth experiments, and assess incrementality, acquisition cost, customer value, and incentive cost. You can distinguish short-term trading volume changes from sustainable growth.

•

An understanding of trading products and their commercial drivers. You are familiar with spot and derivatives fundamentals and how instrument coverage, fees, liquidity, execution quality, and account and position workflows influence customer choice, conversion, and retention. You can translate these factors into product decisions.

•

Experience delivering products that involve technical integration. You have worked with engineers on API or third-party platform integrations and can read interface documentation, understand account authorization and market data, order, and position synchronization, define business rules and acceptance criteria, and drive testing and launch. You connect technical constraints and implementation scope to user value and growth objectives.

•

Strong English communication and cross-functional execution skills. You can work with TradingView partners, marketing, regional, product, and engineering teams on business opportunities, product priorities, and technical feasibility, aligning resources around shared outcomes.

Nice-To-Haves

•

Experience growing a business within TradingView or a comparable trading-tool ecosystem, with examples spanning opportunity discovery, growth validation, and scaling.

•

Experience with trader communities, creators, educational content, partnerships, or channel growth, with the ability to evaluate initiatives by active traders, retention, and revenue contribution.

•

Experience growing products across regions or trader segments, with an understanding of differences in user behavior, customer propositions, and acquisition approaches.

•

Experience with TradingView Broker Integration, Advanced Charts, Trading Platform, or comparable integrations, with an ability to explain how the work improved the user experience or supported growth objectives.

What Success Looks Like

•

An evidence-based growth plan that identifies priority customer segments, OKX's differentiated value, promising distribution channels, and the business opportunity.

•

Validated, repeatable approaches to acquisition, trading conversion, and retention, supported by research and focused experiments that guide engineering investment and resource allocation.

•

Measurable, sustainable growth in active traders, retention, and revenue contribution, with acquisition and incentive costs taken into account.

•

Delivery of the product capabilities and TradingView integrations needed to capture validated opportunities, with improvements to critical user journeys and ongoing measurement of their growth impact.

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

• L&D programs and education subsidy for employees' growth and development

•

Various team building programs and company events

• Wellness and meal allowances

• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

• More that we love to tell you along the process!

Please note that Hong Kong is a group-level service hub, and OKX does not carry on a business of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong.

Crypto.com is one of the world's leading cryptocurrency platforms, serving over 100 million customers globally. Through its acquisition of the North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc. (Nadex), Crypto.com operates a CFTC-regulated designated contract market (FCM/DCM) in the United States, offering derivatives and event contracts to U.S. participants. OG.com, the company's prediction markets platform, extends this regulated infrastructure to event-based trading, positioning the organization at the forefront of the rapidly evolving intersection of digital assets, derivatives, and prediction markets.

The Opportunity
We are seeking a CFO, North Americas to lead the financial function, with responsibility for managing all aspects of finance, audit, tax, accounting and treasury for our U.S. and Canadian entities. This executive will serve as the senior finance leader on the ground in North America, partnering closely with the Group CFO and global finance team while owning the regional financial architecture that supports a CFTC-regulated exchange, a crypto trading platform, a prediction markets business, new business lines, and a NY OCC Trust bank.. The ideal candidate brings a distinctive blend of financial services expertise, public accounting rigor, and hands-on experience in the digital asset industry.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Finance & Leadership

• Own the financial strategy and long-range planning for all Americas entities, including Nadex (DCM), OG.com prediction markets operations, and the U.S. crypto exchange business.

• Serve as the primary finance business partner to Americas leadership, providing data-driven insights on revenue, margin, product economics, and capital allocation.

• Build and present board-ready financial narratives and investor materials as needed.

• Lead annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting, and scenario analysis across all Americas business lines.

• Lead the financial integration and operational setup of new business lines

Financial Reporting & Controls

• Oversee the preparation of U.S. GAAP financial statements, management reporting packages, and consolidation deliverables for global reporting.

• Ensure robust internal controls over financial reporting and SOX-equivalent frameworks as required for a regulated exchange.

• Manage the external audit relationship and coordinate with global finance on group-level audit and statutory requirements.

• Own technical accounting positions on complex topics including digital asset accounting, derivatives revenue recognition, and customer fund segregation.

Regulatory & Compliance Finance

• Ensure financial compliance with CFTC regulations applicable to designated contract markets, including capital adequacy, financial reporting to regulators, and customer protection rules.

• Partner with Legal and Compliance on regulatory filings, examinations, and responses to CFTC, NFA, and state regulatory inquiries.

• Maintain and enhance financial controls for customer fund segregation and protection in accordance with Part 22 and related CFTC requirements.

• Monitor the evolving U.S. regulatory landscape for digital assets and prediction markets, advising leadership on financial and structural implications of new rules.

Treasury & Operations

• Oversee Americas treasury operations, including cash management, bank relationships, and liquidity planning across fiat and digital asset holdings.

• Manage intercompany transactions, transfer pricing, and funding structures between U.S. entities and the global group.

• Collaborate with Tax on federal, state, and international tax planning, compliance, and transfer pricing documentation.

Team Building & Cross-Functional Partnership

• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Americas finance team spanning FP&A, tax, treasury, accounting, and financial operations.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, and Operations to ensure financial considerations are embedded in product launches, market structure changes, and new business initiatives.

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA required.

• 15+ years of progressive finance experience, with a meaningful portion in financial services or capital markets.

• Deep familiarity with US GAAP, including technical accounting for derivatives, financial instruments, and revenue recognition.

• Experience with CFTC-regulated entities or similar regulatory environments (SEC, FINRA, OCC) and the associated financial reporting and capital requirements.

• Proven track record of building and leading finance teams in high-growth, fast-paced environments.

• Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate complex financial topics to senior leadership, board members, and regulators.

Role Overview
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager, Trading to own trading products on the Crypto.com App end-to-end. Retail trading is where users feel the product every day - and where volume, engagement, and retention compound. Every improvement you ship shows up in how people trade, how often they come back, and how Crypto.com wins share in a crowded market.
Your mandate is to drive trading products from discovery through launch and iteration: roadmap clarity, feature definition, customer insight, and shipping at global scale. 
You will run your roadmap with independence within Trading's strategic priorities. You prioritize initiatives, cut tradeoffs, and make the call on what ships when. You report to the Senior Director of Product Management, who sets strategic direction. You own the how and the when.
If you've shipped trading or financial products at scale, this will feel familiar. The difference is you'll be doing it at the frontier of crypto retail trading- perpetuals, spot, and adjacent markets- where the rails keep moving and the playbook is yours to write. No layers. No politics.
 


What You'll Actually Do:
• Own the Trading roadmap. You set milestones, surface dependencies, and keep strategic priorities honest. You make the prioritization call when everything can't ship at once.

• Define and ship trading experiences. You write the specs, run user studies, iterate on feedback, partner with QA on test plans, and clear the backlog. Nothing in your charter goes live without your sign-off.

• Stay close to how traders actually behave. You interview and observe customers. You ask "Show me how you currently trade and manage risk," not "Would you use this feature?" You distinguish what they say from what their behavior reveals.

• Cut the hard tradeoffs. You weigh speed vs. depth, retail clarity vs. power-user needs, and compliance constraints vs. product ambition- and you own the decision.

• Drive market and competitive clarity. You run the research that informs what we build next. Your work shows up in the roadmap, not a slide deck that dies in a folder.

• Represent Trading across the company. You are the DRI in cross-functional forums with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Compliance, and Growth. Alignment is your job; escalation is the exception.

• Own a defined slice of the trading product line. Features in your charter are yours from inception through post-launch iteration. Ownership isn't shipping tickets- it's delivering outcomes.

Job Requirements:
• Crypto and/or perpetuals build experience. You have shipped trading products in crypto and/or perpetuals (not just adjacent fintech). You can point to what you owned, what you launched, and what moved- volume, adoption, retention, or risk/UX outcomes- and what you did when the market or the product broke your assumptions.

• Shipped software or financial products at scale. You have owned customer-facing products end-to-end and can describe a time you coordinated design, eng, and GTM through a launch- and what you did when dependencies slipped.

• Data-informed, user-obsessed. You instrument your own funnel, size opportunities, and prioritize without waiting for someone to hand you the analysis- always through a compassionate lens of the trader.

• Cross-functional leadership without authority. You can describe a time you aligned Design, Engineering, QA, Marketing, Compliance, and Growth toward a ship date, and how you unblocked the team when it stalled.

• AI-native workflow. You demonstrably use AI tools (Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini, LibreChat, or equivalent) with human-in-the-loop judgment. Required, not optional. We care what you've built and owned- not pedigree checkboxes.

Preferred:
•

Stocks, tokenized stocks, and/or options: Hands-on product or market knowledge that accelerates expansion beyond core crypto trading.

•

Retail trading or gamification: You've shipped experiences that make complex markets approachable without dumbing them down.

•

Global consumer product: You've launched and iterated across regions with different regulatory and UX constraints.

Why This Role:
•

Direct product impact. Trading sits on the critical path of how 80M+ users experience Crypto.com. Your work shows up in the numbers.

•

Frontier of retail crypto. Spot, perpetuals, and the next wave of markets- the playbook isn't finished. You'll write parts of it.

•

Autonomy with teeth. You own the roadmap and ship decisions inside a clear strategic frame. Access to the teams that matter. No theater.

•

Growth from within. Crypto.com invests in internal mobility and leadership that develops talent- scope expands with what you deliver.

•

A team that ships. You'll work with ambitious operators across Product, Eng, Design, and Growth who treat ownership as the default.

The enablement team brings together three specialist areas - Workforce Management, Training & Knowledge, and Quality Assurance - and works closely with our regional CX teams, Compliance, Product, Data and our AI and Transformation colleagues.

Day to day, you will drive efficiency across the CX operation - making sure capacity matches demand, agents are ready and supported, and quality is consistently high. Looking further ahead, you will identify and deliver the longer-term opportunities for optimisation, from AI-enabled learning and automated quality assurance to smarter planning for a growing, increasingly digital client base. • Identify recurring gaps or patterns from QC results and highlight areas where further training is needed, working with the relevant teams to close them.

• Lead process improvement initiatives aimed at reducing return rates, simplifying procedures, strengthening first-time-right outcomes across the client lifecycle.
• Serve as a trusted partner to Institutional Sales, Compliance, and Legal, ensuring sustainable business relationships while upholding the Bank's standards.
• Actively contribute to recruitment cycle and performance management to ensure a motivated, high-performing, and accountable team.
• Coach and mentor team members, supporting their skill development and career growth.

• Minimum 5–7 years’ track record in client onboarding, KYC/AML, or compliance operations within the financial services sector.

• Strong knowledge of Swiss regulatory requirements (FINMA, AMLA, CDB) and onboarding / periodic review due diligence standards.
• Experience with remediation exercises, including scoping and delivering ad-hoc reviews arising from audit or compliance testing findings.
• Ability to communicate operational priorities and constraints to technical teams in charge of tooling and systems build-out.
• Experience supporting or participating in audits, preparing business responses.
• Sound risk and quality judgment, with the ability to make independent, defensible decisions on complex cases.
• Ability to prioritize and deliver on multiple tasks in a deadline-driven, high-volume environment.
• Excellent interpersonal skills, results-oriented team player.
• Excellent communication and presentation skills in English and French, German being an advantage.

Additional Information

Summary

Topstep is seeking a hands-on Senior Tax Analyst to support its growing U.S. and international tax function. This individual contributor role will be a key member of the Finance team and will help build a scalable, well-controlled in-house tax compliance function. The role will initially focus on recurring indirect tax compliance across U.S. sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST, EU VAT/OSS, Australia GST, and New Zealand GST, with responsibility expanding as Topstep registers and becomes compliant in additional jurisdictions. The Senior Tax Analyst will work closely with the Tax Director, Accounting, Treasury, People/Payroll, Legal, Operations, Avalara, and external tax advisors to ensure accurate filings, timely payments, complete journal entries and reconciliations, and strong supporting documentation. A key near-term objective is to support the transition of recurring indirect tax compliance in-house beginning with the January 2027 compliance cycle.

Key Responsibilities

• Own and support recurring indirect tax compliance across U.S. sales and use tax, Canada GST/HST, EU VAT/OSS, Australia GST, New Zealand GST, and additional jurisdictions as the compliance footprint expands.

• Support the transition of recurring indirect tax compliance from external providers to the internal tax function beginning with the January 2027 compliance cycle.

• Prepare monthly and quarterly tax returns and supporting workpapers; ensure filings and related tax payments are completed accurately and on time.

• Extract, validate, and reconcile tax data from NetSuite, Avalara, payment processors, and other source systems, and investigate differences between tax collected, reported, paid, and general ledger balances.

• Prepare indirect tax journal entries, accruals, true-ups, and balance sheet account reconciliations, and maintain complete filing and payment support.

• Maintain the tax compliance calendar, registrations, filing frequencies, portal access, tax IDs, deadlines, and filing/payment confirmations.

• Coordinate with Avalara and external advisors on filings, data requests, notices, registrations, taxability matters, and open compliance issues.

• Assist with responses to state, federal, and international tax notices, audits, and information requests, including maintaining an organized record of correspondence and resolutions.

• Coordinate data gathering and workpaper support for federal, state, and international direct tax compliance, including returns, extensions, estimated payments, and tax provision support performed with external advisors.

• Provide support to People/Payroll on state tax registrations, payroll tax notices, withholding compliance, and related filings as needed.

• Research taxability, nexus, filing requirements, and new jurisdiction obligations and support implementation of new registrations and compliance processes.

• Identify opportunities to improve tax processes, documentation, controls, and automation, including effective use of Avalara, NetSuite, and other tax technology.

• Partner with Finance, Accounting, Legal, Treasury, People/Payroll, and Operations on tax-related matters and support forecasting, exposure analyses, and other ad hoc tax projects.

Required Qualifications and Key Competencies

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field.

• 4-7 years of progressive tax experience in a corporate, public accounting, or advisory environment.

• Strong hands-on tax compliance, reconciliation, and Excel skills, with the ability to manage recurring monthly and quarterly deadlines across multiple jurisdictions.

• Experience with U.S. sales and use tax and/or international VAT/GST compliance strongly preferred.

• Experience with Avalara and NetSuite, including tax data extraction, reconciliation, or compliance workflows, strongly preferred.

• Experience supporting corporate income tax compliance and coordinating with external tax advisors preferred.

• CPA, EA, MST, or similar tax/accounting credential preferred but not required.

• Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with high attention to detail and accountability for personal deliverables.

• Ability to operate as a hands-on individual contributor, prioritize competing deadlines, document processes, and collaborate effectively across Finance, Accounting, Legal, Treasury, People/Payroll, Operations, and external advisors.

Company Culture & Perks

• Topstep is an engaging working environment that ranges from fully remote to hybrid. We foster a culture of collaboration by keeping cameras on during meetings and maintaining a robust Slack environment for communication.

• Seven Company-paid Holidays and generous Family Leave. Paid time off is front-loaded.

• Competitive 401(k) matching, health, dental, and vision insurance are offered for full-time employees.

• Vacations are encouraged with a bonus for taking 5 consecutive days. Topstep offers a food and groceries budget and contributes towards health and wellness.

New Hire Base Salary Range

• $95,000.00 - $120,000.00 annually.

• The compensation offered will take into account the internal compensation structure and may vary depending on the candidate's geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, among other factors.

• This position is eligible for a performance-based bonus as provided by the plan terms and governing documents.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Topstep is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all employees and applicants are valued. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status, in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Interested in the role? Apply today with your resume!

Risk and control framework

Map controls to processes, risks and applicable obligations. Identify control gaps, duplicate controls, outdated records and missing ownership for review.

•

Support Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) cycles by collecting inputs, checking completeness and recording changes to risks, controls and action plans.

Evidence and control testing

•

Request and organise evidence from control owners across departments, maintain an accessible audit trail and follow up on overdue submissions.

Perform sample-based second-line testing under an approved test plan, assessing control design and operating effectiveness as applicable.

Issues and remediation

Record control deficiencies and agreed actions with clear descriptions, owners, due dates and status; follow up on overdue or recurring issues.

•

Review evidence of completed actions and, where required, retest before recommending closure. Escalate unresolved matters through the agreed process.

Cross-department control monitoring dashboards

Build and maintain dashboards that monitor key controls across departments against agreed thresholds, including control performance, overdue evidence, testing exceptions, open issues and remediation timeliness.

Work with risk and control owners to document approved indicators, thresholds, data sources, review frequency and escalation triggers. Check that dashboard data is consistent, complete and traceable to the underlying records.

•

Monitor threshold breaches and adverse trends, investigate anomalies with control owners, and escalate exceptions with clear context and action status through periodic risk reports and governance meetings.

GRC records and audit support

•

Keep risk, control, process, evidence and issue records current in the GRC tool; run data quality checks and prepare standard reporting extracts.

•

Prepare relevant records and evidence for internal audit, external audit and regulatory reviews in coordination with the wider team.

Attention to the details and result oriented

One to three years of relevant experience in operational risk, internal controls, internal audit, compliance or a regulated operating environment.

Strong Excel skills, including the ability to consolidate and check data, use formulas and pivot tables, and build clear dashboards or management reports.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Software Engineer to join our Payments Team, based in the Hong Kong. Payments is where OKX meets the real financial world. Our team has built and operates the infrastructure connecting OKX to dozens of payment channels across global markets, giving users deposit and withdrawal options that are fast, convenient, and — most importantly — trustworthy. That platform moves and safeguards user assets at institutional scale, continuously, across time zones and regulatory environments.

This is not a greenfield team looking for its footing. The team is established, the platform is in production at scale, and we are actively expanding — both in scope and in headcount. That combination is rare: you get the leverage of joining a growing team where your work visibly shifts the roadmap, along with the discipline that comes from a system already trusted with real money.

It's also an unusually good place to learn. Payments is a domain that's hard to pick up from the outside — every market has its own rails, its own settlement behavior, its own failure modes, its own compliance expectations. Here you'll work across a wide range of payment methods and channels, and you'll build the judgment that comes from operating financial systems where the stakes are real: how to design for correctness when money is on the line, how to reconcile, how to recover, how to keep a platform observable enough that you find problems before your users do.

You'll work closely with product managers, designers, and partner-facing teams, and you'll set the technical bar for the engineers around you — through design docs, code reviews, and the everyday habit of doing things properly when nobody's watching.

If you like the sound of a team where the problems are genuinely hard, the standard is high, and your opinion changes the outcome, we'd like to talk.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Design and build the core. Develop high-scale, 24/7 APIs and distributed payment services across multiple cloud providers, using Java and Spring Boot as the primary stack. Own systems end to end — from design doc through production ownership.

•

Expand our global reach. Help integrate and scale new payment channels and methods across markets, each with its own technical, operational, and reliability characteristics.

•

Protect user assets. Build for correctness first: consistency, idempotency, reconciliation, failure recovery, and the operational tooling that lets us stand behind every transaction.

•

Set the technical bar. Participate actively in design and code reviews, giving and receiving direct, constructive feedback. Help evolve the standards a growing team builds on.

•

Solve the hard problems. Investigate complex distributed-systems challenges and drive them to resolution rather than handing them off.

•

Partner across functions. Work with product, design, and partner teams across regions to turn ambiguous requirements into shipped systems, and to unblock dependencies before they become delays.

•

Grow the team's capability. Mentor engineers and share what you learn. Seniority here is measured in leverage, not just output.

•

Stay curious. Keep pace with a fast-moving industry and bring the good ideas back.

What you'll take away from this role

•

Deep, practical fluency across a wide range of global payment methods and channels — knowledge that is genuinely hard to acquire anywhere else

•

Experience designing and operating systems entrusted with substantial user assets, where correctness and recoverability are non-negotiable

•

A track record of shipping in a regulated, high-stakes domain at real scale

• 8+ years of backend software development experience, with a proven track record of building and operating high-availability, large-scale applications.

• Strong engineering fundamentals — data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and software design patterns — and the judgment to know when to reach for which.

• Ownership instinct. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just tickets. When something's broken or unclear, you move toward it.

• Partner with FCP and AML subject-matter experts on transaction monitoring, customer segmentation, scenario development, client risk rating, surveillance support, and AML-related development initiatives that strengthen financial crime prevention capabilities.

• Practical experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Kafka, Snowflake, Airflow, Azure, or similar technologies.

• Experience with financial crime prevention in regulated financial services, including AML, KYC/CDD/ODD, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, client risk rating, and market-abuse surveillance support.
• Experience with GDPR-sensitive data, audit evidence, regulator-facing reporting, or data governance in control-heavy environments.
• Nice to have: experience with data quality validation tools e.g. Great Expectations (GX), dbt‑expectations, Soda, Deequ, or Microsoft Fabric.

order execution flows

market data distribution

risk calculations

trading cores

pricing engines

real-time message pipelines

Detect bottlenecks, resource leaks, deadlocks

Maintain and improve AI framework.

concurrent systems

distributed microservices

event-driven architectures

API (REST, gRPC, GraphQL)

functional testing, integration testing, regression testing, performance testing, non-functional requirements.

About IG
IG is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof.

Your role in the Team

We're looking for a Senior Platform Engineer with deep Akamai expertise to own IG's edge delivery estate and change how it's run.
Today, much of our Akamai configuration is managed by hand through Control Center. Your mandate is to move it into code: Terraform modules, version-controlled rule trees, and GitLab pipelines with the automated checks and guardrails that let application teams request and ship their own edge changes safely. You'll be the expert other engineers come to, and the person who steadily reduces how often they need to.
The Platform Team owns the infrastructure and automation platform underpinning IG's global trading operations – cloud-native infrastructure on AWS, GitLab CI/CD, and self-service capabilities that help development teams move faster with greater confidence. Edge delivery sits at the very front of that stack: every customer session, trade, and API call reaches IG through it, across every region we operate in and under latency-sensitive conditions.
You'll work hands-on with Property Manager and Akamai's rule tree model, Edge DNS and traffic management, edge security controls, and certificate lifecycle – from routine property changes through to incident diagnosis and long-term modernisation of the estate. If you care about content delivery and edge infrastructure, and want your work to have direct commercial and customer impact, we'd welcome your application.

What you'll do

Automate the estate and enable self-service
• Lead the migration of Akamai configuration from manual Control Center changes to a Terraform-first workflow, building reusable, well-documented modules for properties, rule trees, and DNS that other teams can safely consume
• Build self-service paths for routine edge changes – new hostnames, redirects, caching rules – wrapped in policy checks, automated validation, and staging tests that catch mistakes before they reach production
• Integrate edge configuration into GitLab CI/CD alongside ServiceNow change control, so every property and DNS change is peer-reviewed, tested, and promoted through environments the same way each time
• Build tooling around Akamai's APIs (Python, Bash) that removes repetitive operational work – bulk changes, certificate expiry checks, drift detection, and inventory reporting
Own edge delivery and routing
• Own the design, configuration, and operational health of IG's Akamai estate across staging and production networks, in line with change control
• Design and maintain URL redirection, rewrite, and forwarding logic – 301/302, host- and path-based, and Cloudlet-driven – across IG's public and internal domains, rationalising inherited redirect chains as you go
• Configure routing and origin behaviour, including edge hostnames, CP codes, conditional and dynamic origin selection, failover, and load balancing to support multi-origin, multi-region delivery
• Set caching and delivery strategy – compression, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, image and video delivery, API acceleration – and run purge and cache invalidation workflows that support release and incident response
• Support multi-CDN and failover strategy through Global Traffic Management, and contribute to disaster recovery and resilience planning for edge delivery
Secure and govern the edge
• Configure and tune edge security controls – Site Shield, network lists and IP allow-listing, WAF, and bot mitigation – as traffic patterns and threats evolve
• Manage the SSL/TLS certificate lifecycle for edge properties in coordination with Venafi, ensuring certificates reach the edge well ahead of expiry
• Maintain an auditable inventory of properties, hostnames, certificates, and CP codes, and lead periodic reviews that surface and remediate configuration drift and stale entries
Diagnose, partner, and share
• Diagnose complex delivery, routing, and performance incidents using Edge Diagnostics, debug and pragma headers, mPulse, and reporting APIs – tracing an issue from DNS resolution through edge and origin behaviour to root cause, then closing the gap that allowed it
• Partner with Platform Managers and application teams to translate hosting and delivery requirements into configuration that is secure, performant, and maintainable, and spread edge knowledge across the wider platform organisation

What you'll need

Experience level: 5+ years in CDN and edge delivery engineering, with deep hands-on Akamai expertise and a strong infrastructure-as-code background.
• Deep Akamai expertise – property creation, versioning, rule tree configuration, and activation across staging and production via Property Manager (Control Center and PAPI), with the judgement to know which logic belongs at the edge and which doesn't
• Automation and infrastructure-as-code – hands-on with the Akamai Terraform Provider, writing reusable modules that others actually adopt; GitLab CI/CD pipeline experience; and scripting in Python or Bash to automate against vendor APIs
• Routing, DNS, and traffic management – edge hostnames, CP codes, origin and failover behaviour, conditional origins, and traffic steering, with working knowledge of Edge DNS and/or Global Traffic Management for resolution, load balancing, and multi-region routing
• Redirection and rewrite strategy – host- and path-based redirects, rewrites, and Cloudlet policies (Edge Redirector, Forward Rewrite, Visitor Prioritization), including untangling legacy redirect logic without breaking live traffic
• Edge security and certificates – Site Shield, network lists, WAF and bot mitigation, plus SSL/TLS certificate lifecycle management (ideally with Venafi) and a solid grasp of certificate chains, SNI, and secure delivery requirements
• Troubleshooting and delivery observability – Edge Diagnostics, debug headers, mPulse (RUM), and traffic reporting APIs, backed by strong network fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, routing) and a clear picture of how DNS, CDN, origin, and application layers interact under production load
• Delivering change in a controlled environment – experience working through formal ITSM/change-control processes such as ServiceNow, in regulated or high-availability settings
Nice to have
• Akamai certification in Web Performance, Cloud Security, or Media Delivery
• Other CDN and edge platforms (CloudFront, Cloudflare, Fastly) for comparative or multi-CDN architecture
• AWS networking services (Route 53, CloudFront, ALB/NLB) and hybrid CDN-to-cloud-origin patterns
• Edge compute (EdgeWorkers/EdgeKV), API Gateway, or service mesh for application-layer traffic management
• Akamai DataStream or similar for streaming delivery telemetry into wider observability tooling
• Compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS as they apply to edge and CDN configuration

What makes you stand out

You troubleshoot systematically, tracing an issue from DNS resolution through edge routing, caching, and origin behaviour rather than reacting to surface-level symptoms. You've modernised a CDN estate before – cleaning up legacy properties, redirect chains, and routing rules without destabilising high-traffic, latency-sensitive applications.
The automation you build gets used. Whether it's Terraform modules, API-driven pipelines, or self-service workflows, it's robust, well-documented, and genuinely adopted by the teams who depend on it – because you designed it around how they actually work, and put guardrails in place that make the safe path the easy one.
Security and compliance aren't an afterthought for you. You've tuned WAF rules, managed certificate lifecycle, and hardened edge configuration, and you understand how choices made at the edge shape risk. You're equally comfortable owning a single complex property change and setting the routing and redirection strategy for an entire domain estate – and you're methodical enough to balance immediate operational demands against longer-term platform quality.

The Perks
Your growth fuels our success! Thrive with tailored development programs, mentoring opportunities with leaders, and clear career progression. Expand your network through committees, sports and social clubs. Enjoy extra time off for volunteering and community work.

• Own the solution architecture and high-level design for Post Trade regulatory reporting data — from trade and lifecycle event capture on the enterprise message bus, through the lakehouse layers, to submission, acknowledgement handling and reconciliation against trade repositories.

Dimensional and canonical modelling, conformed dimensions, slowly changing dimensions, grain determination, and the trade-off between nested and repeated structures versus normalised models in BigQuery. Design to the enterprise canonical standard — extending it through the governance forum where a domain genuinely needs something it does not cover.
• Own schema contracts in practice. Avro schema design and review; compatibility mode selection (backward, forward, full and their transitive variants) and the producer/consumer upgrade ordering each one implies; union and default-value design for evolvability; topic, key, partition and compaction design; and the operational consequences of getting any of those wrong.
• Design ingestion for both batch and streaming. Watermarks, windowing, triggers and allowed lateness for out-of-order arrival; replay and restatement; idempotency and deduplication strategy; dead-letter and poison-message handling; and honest reasoning about where exactly-once guarantees actually stop — they do not extend past the Kafka boundary to an external sink.
• Build data quality and profiling into the design — DQ gates at layer boundaries, reconciliation and break detection, completeness and accuracy controls, and the lineage and audit evidence that regulated consumers, internal audit and regulators will ask for.
• Apply the governance model. PII classification, BigQuery policy tags, column-level and row-level security, dynamic data masking, IAM/RBAC design, CMEK and key management — including the design tension where privacy obligations and multi-year regulatory retention pull in opposite directions.
• Work with infrastructure and platform engineering to specify and guide the setup of the runtimes the data architecture requires.
• Produce the artefacts and take them through review. HLDs, interface specifications, ADRs and reference designs, authored to a standard that survives formal architecture governance and your own absence from the room.
• Work across teams — with producing service teams on event contracts, with data and database engineering, messaging and data science, and with business and compliance stakeholders on what the data has to mean.
• Contribute to the architecture - design reviews, standards feedback, knowledge sharing, and mentoring engineers into architectural thinking.

• Post Trade or regulatory reporting data experience. Direct delivery experience on at least one of MiFIR, EMIR (including Refit), ASIC, MAS, SFTR or CFTC reporting. Reportable-event determination, lifecycle and correction semantics, identifier management (UTI, UPI, LEI, ISIN), pairing and matching, reconciliation against trade repository acknowledgements and rejections, back-reporting, and a working grasp of what a completeness or accuracy breach actually costs to remediate.
• Deep, hands-on GCP. BigQuery is the centre of gravity: partitioning and clustering strategy, slot reservations and cost governance, authorised views and datasets, materialised views, table snapshots and time travel, the Storage Write API, policy tags, column-level and row-level security, dynamic data masking, and CMEK. Plus Cloud Composer/Airflow (idempotent task design, backfill and catch-up semantics), Dataflow or Dataproc, Datastream for change data capture, GCS, Cloud Run and Cloud Functions, Pub/Sub, IAM, VPC Service Controls, and Dataplex for classification, data quality and lineage. GCP depth is what we are hiring for; breadth on other clouds is welcome but does not substitute for it.
• Medallion lakehouse design in production — Bronze/Silver/Gold with immutability at Bronze, progressive quality enforcement, deterministic reprocessing, and a defensible position on where transformation logic is allowed to live.
• Kafka at enterprise scale with a governed schema registry (Cloudera, Confluent or equivalent) — Avro schema design and evolution, compatibility modes and their operational consequences, event-driven ingestion into a cloud data platform, consumer group and lag management, compacted topics and tombstone semantics, and the ordering and delivery guarantees Kafka does and does not provide.
• Data governance in a regulated environment — IAM/RBAC frameworks, PII classification and encryption, data retention design, audit logging, and compliance-driven design under FCA, GDPR or equivalent supervision.
• Architecture artefacts that have passed formal review — HLDs, ADRs, interface specifications, reference designs. You can evaluate competing options, articulate trade-offs without hedging, decide under ambiguity, and write the decision down.

• Working command of core data platform concepts — data lake, ODS, data warehouse and lakehouse — and a clear view of when each is the right answer rather than a default.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

 

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

We are looking for an Affiliate Growth Lead, US to build and scale our relationships with finance and investing creators and affiliates across the US market. The role combines business development, creator and affiliate partnerships and performance marketing, with a clear commercial mandate: drive attributable funded accounts and trading volume from active traders and investors, starting with Margin.

 

This is not a crypto-native KOL role. The audience we want to reach already trades and invests, and we reach them through the creators and publishers they trust in traditional finance, trading education and wealth management.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own business development for US finance and investing creators and affiliates, building a high-quality pipeline of trading educators, finance YouTubers and podcasters, newsletter authors, and wealth-management and advisor-creators.

 - Develop and execute the US creator and affiliate strategy, starting with a focus on driving Margin trading volume and funded accounts, with the scope to expand across Kraken's other trading products.

 - Own partner acquisition and relationship development, from initial outreach and commercial conversations through activation and ongoing growth.

 - Structure CPA, revenue-share and hybrid partnerships that tie partner incentives to funded accounts and trading activity.

 - Set up and manage the tracking, attribution, payout and reporting needed to measure partners through funded and traded accounts.

 - Work with Legal and Compliance on disclosure, content review and approved messaging, so that promotion of leveraged products is responsible and consistent.

 - Partner across Growth, Marketing, Product and other relevant teams to turn creator and affiliate opportunities into effective campaigns, and bring partner and audience feedback back into the product.

 - Coordinate with the NORAM Pro KOL Business Development team so each creator has a single point of contact and relationships are not duplicated.

 - Track attributable trading volume, funded accounts, active-trader retention and CAC per partner, and use the results to prioritize partners and investment.

 - Continuously identify emerging creators, communities and affiliate publishers that reach active traders and investors in the US.

 
 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Deep experience in business development, partnerships, influencer management or affiliate-led growth in the US, with a track record of running performance-based creator or affiliate programs for a brokerage, trading platform or investing product.

 - Experience growing margin, options, futures or other leveraged or active-trading products.

 - A strong existing network and understanding of the US finance and investing creator ecosystem, including trading educators, finance YouTubers, newsletter authors, podcasters and wealth-management or advisor-creators.

 - Working knowledge of crypto and digital assets, with the ability to explain crypto trading products clearly to audiences who are new to them.

 - Demonstrated ability to originate, negotiate and grow commercially meaningful partnerships, including CPA, revenue-share and hybrid deal structures.

 - Hands-on experience with affiliate networks and tracking platforms.

 - A record of turning creator or affiliate activity into measurable outcomes such as funded accounts, trading volume, revenue or acquisition, with results you can describe in numbers.

 - Familiarity with US financial advertising rules, including FTC paid-endorsement disclosure, and experience getting creator content through compliance review.

 - Strong relationship-building skills, with the credibility to work with creators who protect their audience's trust and are selective about the brands they promote.

 - Commercial judgment: you prioritize partners based on expected impact on conversion and trading activity, not on reach or activity alone.

 - Comfort using performance data to evaluate partners, diagnose results, adjust strategy and end partnerships that do not perform.

 - Strong cross-functional execution skills and the ability to move opportunities from prospecting through launch and ongoing growth.

 
 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience working in wealth management or fintech.

 - Experience at a crypto exchange or digital-asset firm.

 - Existing relationships with US crypto-native creators.





Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We’re hiring a Product Manager with deep UX and interaction design expertise to build social experiences around investing and trading at Kraken.


You should be comfortable designing flows yourself, building interactive prototypes, and working through interaction details with designers and engineers. You’ll also own the product decisions: which customer problem to solve, what to ship first, and how to measure whether the experience improved.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Design complete social journeys. Work through how someone discovers a person, decides to follow them, shares an idea or trade, receives a response, and returns. Connect these interactions into an experience users understand without explanation.

 - Make the interaction details work. Shape navigation, information hierarchy, copy, defaults, gestures, and feedback. Specify what happens when a feed is empty, a post fails, content loads slowly, or someone changes their mind.

 - Prototype before committing to a build. Turn ideas into interactive prototypes that communicate the intended behavior. Explore alternatives, test the uncertain parts, and give engineering clear flows, states, and acceptance criteria.

 - Use psychology to improve participation. Understand why people hesitate to post, seek recognition, follow strangers, or respond to others. Translate those motivations into decisions about audience visibility, prompts, reputation, feedback, and the effort required to contribute.

 - Observe users and fix what gets in their way. Run usability sessions, watch people complete tasks, and combine those observations with funnel data. Identify where people misunderstand the product, lose confidence, or abandon an action.

 - Design for first use and repeated use. Make the experience useful before someone has connections. Keep sharing lightweight during an active trading session, with clear control over what becomes public. Test the twentieth interaction as carefully as the first.

 - Connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. For each significant change, define the expected behavior and how to test it. Track task completion, abandonment, first follows, first contributions, responses, and subsequent retention. Work with data science to evaluate experiments and effects on both contributors and their audiences.

 - Take the experience through launch. Choose a focused initial scope, resolve trade-offs with engineering, review the implementation against the intended design, and use post-launch evidence to decide what to improve next.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Has designed and shipped consumer social experiences. Your portfolio shows your contribution to feeds, profiles, sharing, messaging, discovery, or communities—and how the experience changed after launch.

 - Has strong interaction design craft. You can explain why a flow is structured a particular way, what users will notice first, what they need to understand, and which decisions or steps can be removed.

 - Can build realistic interactive prototypes. You use Figma, code, AI tools, or a combination to make behavior tangible and testable, including transitions, empty states, and failure states.

 - Understands behavior through evidence. You can show where user research challenged your assumptions and changed a design.

 - Can own product outcomes. You can prioritize a problem, define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and explain whether an experiment produced a meaningful improvement.

 - Understands the context of social finance. You account for how credibility, incentives, reputation, and visibility of financial activity affect what people trust and choose to share.

Ndax is a Canadian cryptocurrency trading platform headquartered in Calgary, Alberta. We are registered with the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) as an investment dealer and operate as a marketplace. We're looking for an experienced Fractional Chief Information Security Officer (vCISO) to lead our information security program on a part-time basis.
You'll own our security program end to end and lead our internal security team. You'll work directly with the CEO and leadership to set security direction, meet our regulatory obligations, and protect our platform, our clients, and the digital assets we hold in custody.
This role suits a security leader who already serves other clients and wants to make a real impact in a regulated fintech and digital asset environment.

Key responsibilities:
Leadership and strategy
• Lead, manage, and mentor our internal security team
• Own our information security strategy and multi-year roadmap
• Assess our current security posture and identify gaps, risks, and priorities
• Report security risks, metrics, and program progress to executives and the board
Governance, risk, and compliance
• Build and maintain security policies, standards, procedures, and controls
• Keep us compliant with Canadian securities, AML, and privacy requirements, including CIRO, the CSA, FINTRAC, PIPEDA, and Alberta's PIPA
• Lead audit readiness for SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar frameworks, and act as the security point of contact for auditors and regulators
• Oversee vendor and third-party risk, including custodians, cloud providers, and key technology partners
Platform and digital asset security
• Set security standards for custody, wallet infrastructure, and cryptographic key management
• Guide cloud, application, and identity and access security across our trading platform
• Oversee vulnerability management, penetration testing, and threat monitoring
Resilience and culture
• Develop, test, and maintain incident response and business continuity plans
• Lead the response to security incidents, including regulatory notifications where required
• Drive security awareness and training across the company
Requirements
Required
• 10+ years in information security, including at least 5 years in a CISO, vCISO, or head of security role
• Experience leading security programs at a regulated financial services, fintech, or digital asset company
• Working knowledge of Canadian regulatory expectations for registered dealers and money services businesses (CIRO, CSA, FINTRAC) and Canadian privacy law
• Hands-on experience taking an organization through SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits
• Track record of building incident response programs and leading real incidents
• Experience managing and developing security staff
• Clear communicator who can brief a board as comfortably as an engineering team
Nice to have
• Experience securing cryptocurrency custody, hot and cold wallet operations, or HSM and MPC key management
• Familiarity with NIST CSF, CIS Controls, or CCSS (Cryptocurrency Security Standard)
• Background in cloud security (AWS or Azure) and securing trading or payments platforms
• Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, or CCSK
Engagement details
• Fractional, part-time independent contractor engagement
• Hours tracked and invoiced monthly
• Reachable for urgent security incidents outside regular hours, as agreed in the contract
• Expected to sign a confidentiality agreement and pass a background check before starting
