OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on and commercially minded Senior Compliance Manager to join our Product Compliance team.This is a senior individual-contributor role focused primarily on the day-to-day review of new products, material product changes and existing product enhancements. The emphasis is on delivering timely, well-reasoned product compliance assessments using a risk-based approach, ensuring that material compliance risks are sufficiently mitigated and the firm’s regulatory positioning protected.You will act as a trusted compliance partner throughout the product development lifecycle, helping Product and Engineering teams navigate complex regulatory requirements while enabling commercially viable outcomes. You will be expected to distinguish between legal or regulatory constraints that cannotbe crossed, risks that can be addressed through proportionate controls, and residual risks that require documented escalation or risk acceptance.

What You'll Be Doing

•

Own and deliver day-to-day compliance reviews of new products, features, market expansions and material changes to existing products across OKX's global business and product suite

•

Review product requirements, technical documentation, user journeys, onboarding flows, trading or transaction mechanics, reward structures, disclosures and operational processes.

•

Apply a risk-based waterfall that distinguishes hard legal or regulatory blockers from risks that may be addressed through controls, product conditions, jurisdictional restrictions, monitoring orescalation.

• Conduct and document product compliance risk assessments covering areas such as regulatory perimeter and licensing, AML/CFT, sanctions, KYC, consumer protection, financial promotions, trading and market conduct, asset safeguarding, data privacy and third-party risk.

• Produce clear, concise and evidence-based and solutions-based compliance recommendations setting out identified risks, required mitigants, residual exposure and the proposed approval or escalation route.

• Work directly with Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, Central Compliance and local Compliance teams to develop practical and scalable solutions to identified compliance requirements.

• Maintain complete and accurate documentation and audit trails for product reviews, decisions, conditions, exceptions, approvals and subsequent changes.

• Support post-launch monitoring, control testing and assurance in partnership with Audit, Product and other Compliance teams, and drive remediation of identified issues

• Promote a compliance-by-design culture within the product lifecycle; communicate the Product Compliance framework and program requirements to relevant stakeholders and deliver targeted training or guidance to Product, Engineering and business teams as required.

• Support special projects and priority product launches in a fast-paced and continually evolving environment.

What We Look For In You

•

At least 8 years of relevant experience in Compliance, Legal or Risk within financial services, fintech, payments or the cryptocurrency industry.

•

Bachelor's degree in law, finance, business, economics, engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

• Significant hands-on experience in product compliance, regulatory advisory or product risk assessment, including advising on new products and material product changes

• Strong understanding of the digital-asset industry and the products offered by crypto platforms, including trading, custody, payments, staking or earn products, lending, structured products, wallets or DeFi.

• Strong working knowledge of relevant regulatory and compliance requirements, including licensing and regulatory-perimeter considerations, AML/CFT, sanctions, KYC, consumer protection, financial promotions and trading or market-conduct requirements.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze products or initiatives involving significant complexity and risk and translate regulatory requirements into practical product requirements and controls.

• Experience in and demonstrated success in leveraging AI-enabled technology to maintain risk assessment standards, including ongoing tuning of agentic skills aligned with the Company’s risk appetite.

• Excellent risk judgment and the ability to balance compliance rigor with a pragmatic, risk-based approach that supports responsible commercial outcomes.

• Proven ability to develop and deliver repeatable product compliance solutions, controls and review processes aligned with broader group requirements.

• Strong project-management and execution skills, including the ability to manage multiple concurrent reviews, maintain accurate documentation and meet product-launch deadlines

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clear recommendations and lead discussions with Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, senior management and other Compliance stakeholders.

• Strong stakeholder-management skills and the ability to influence product decisions and constructively challenge proposals without compromising Compliance rigor.

• Self-motivated, proactive and comfortable operating independently within a fast-paced, globallydispersed team.

• High personal integrity and sound professional judgment, including the ability to identify when an issue requires escalation

Nice to Haves

• Direct product compliance or regulatory advisory experience at a crypto exchange, fintech or technology-led financial-services company.

• Experience supporting multi-jurisdictional product launches and applying regulatory requirements across the United States, European Union, Middle East or Asia-Pacific

• Practical knowledge of CeFi trading products, including spot, derivatives, leverage, custody, institutional products and OTC flows

• Familiarity with Web3 products, blockchain technology, smart contracts, DeFi protocols and digital-asset transaction flows.

• Experience developing compliance risk-assessment frameworks, controls, and key risk indicators

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

•

Various team building programs and company events

•

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

•

More that we love to tell you along the process!

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

•

The salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. In addition to the salary, a performance bonus and long-term incentives may be provided as part of the compensation package, as well as a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. Applicants should apply via OKX internal or external careers site.

Notice:

All official OKX vacancies are published on this website. While roles may appear on selected third-party platforms from time to time, information on other sites may be inaccurate or outdated. If in doubt, please apply directly through our official careers website.

Information collected and processed as part of the recruitment process of any job application you choose to submit is subject to OKX's Candidate Privacy Notice.

• This role requires more than strong settlement operational experience. The ideal candidate should have a solid understanding of trading and settlement system architecture, including how settlement systems interact with trading platforms, transaction data, custody/banking infrastructure, and finance/accounting systems.

• The role will serve as a key bridge between Finance, Settlement Operations, Product, Engineering, and other relevant stakeholders, translating settlement and accounting requirements into clear system, data, and reporting requirements.

• Candidates with experience in traditional financial markets, securities, banking, brokerage, clearing, custody, or other transaction-intensive financial institutions are highly preferred.

• The successful candidate will build a settlement and reconciliation function that is not only operationally effective, but also system-driven, highly reconcilable, and finance-ready.

• The individual should be able to understand a transaction from execution through settlement, reconciliation, and ultimately financial accounting, and work across Operations, Finance, Product, Data, and Engineering to ensure that the underlying processes and systems are scalable, controlled, and transparent.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Settlement Operations
- Lead and oversee day-to-day settlement operations across digital asset and fiat transactions.
- Ensure transactions are settled accurately, completely, and within the required timelines.
- Establish and continuously improve settlement procedures, controls, exception handling, and escalation mechanisms.
- Identify settlement breaks, operational risks, and process inefficiencies, and drive timely resolution.
- Support new products, transaction flows, and business models by assessing their settlement and operational requirements.

• Settlement System & System Architecture
- Develop a strong understanding of the end-to-end settlement system architecture and transaction data flow.
- Understand how settlement systems interface with:
- Trading systems and order/transaction engines;
- Wallet, custody, and blockchain infrastructure;
- Fiat banking and payment systems;
- Data warehouse and reporting platforms; and
- Finance, accounting, and general ledger systems.
- Work closely with Product and Engineering teams to define settlement-related system requirements.
- Translate operational and finance requirements into clear and actionable data, system, and reporting specifications for Engineering teams.
- Define the reports, data fields, transaction-level information, and reconciliation logic required to support settlement operations and financial accounting.
- Participate in system implementation, enhancement, UAT, and post-implementation validation from a settlement and finance-control perspective.

•

Digital Asset Reconciliation
- Own and oversee Digital Asset (DA) reconciliation, including reconciliation among customer balances, internal ledgers, wallet/on-chain balances, custody records, and other relevant source systems.
- Investigate and resolve reconciliation differences, including transaction timing differences, system exceptions, missing transactions, and data inconsistencies.
- Work with Product, Engineering, Data, Wallet, and Finance teams to identify root causes and implement sustainable remediation.
- Establish appropriate reconciliation controls and monitoring mechanisms to ensure completeness and accuracy of digital asset balances and movements.

• Fiat Reconciliation
- Own and oversee Fiat reconciliation across customer balances, banking/custodian records, payment channels, internal operational systems, and the general ledger.
- Ensure customer fiat assets and liabilities can be reconciled to relevant operational and accounting records.
- Investigate reconciliation breaks and coordinate with Finance, Fiat Operations, Product, Engineering, banks, custodians, and payment service providers for resolution.
- Drive automation and system improvements to reduce manual reconciliation and operational dependency.

• Customer Transaction Reconciliation
- Oversee transaction-level reconciliation covering customer trades, deposits, withdrawals, transfers, settlements, and other relevant transaction activities.
- Ensure customer transaction records can be traced consistently across trading, settlement, operational, and accounting systems.
- Establish effective exception-management processes for unmatched or incomplete transactions.
- Support Finance and external audit requirements by ensuring transaction data and reconciliation evidence are complete, accurate, and traceable.

• Finance & Accounting Support
- Partner closely with Finance to ensure settlement data and reports provide sufficient information for accurate and timely accounting.
- Understand how trading and settlement activities ultimately flow into financial records and the general ledger.
- Define operational reports and data outputs required by Finance for:
- Accounting entries;
- Period-end closing;
- Balance sheet reconciliation;
- Customer asset and liability reconciliation; and
- Financial and external audit support.
- Identify gaps between operational systems and accounting requirements and work with relevant teams to develop scalable solutions.

• Process, Control & Team Management
- Build and maintain robust settlement and reconciliation SOPs, controls, and governance frameworks.
- Drive automation and process improvements to improve settlement efficiency, accuracy, scalability, and control.
- Establish key operational metrics and monitor settlement exceptions, reconciliation breaks, aging items, and resolution timelines.

In 2018, Bitvavo launched the first version of its digital assets trading platform, to bridge the gap between traditional currencies and digital assets. By offering transparent fees, a wide range of assets and an easy to use platform, Bitvavo is making the currency of the future accessible for everyone.

In eight years time, Bitvavo has established itself as the market leader in the Netherlands and one of the largest in Europe, with over two million users exchanging tens of billions of digital assets a year.


ABOUT THE ROLE

People trust Bitvavo with their money, their digital assets and their personal data. Your job is to make sure that trust is always deserved.

We are seeking a strong Data Protection Officer to drive and continuously develop Bitvavo's data protection program, ensuring compliance with data protection and privacy laws including the GDPR. Reporting to the Head of Legal, you will work closely with multiple business units and products to keep Bitvavo compliant across all areas of data protection, as part of the legal team based in Amsterdam. You will own the business processes and policies covering data access, classification, quality and life cycle management.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone ready to lead the DPO function independently, comfortable making decisions and engaging directly with regulators and with stakeholders at every level, including our Management Board.


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

This role requires a broad understanding of data protection law, including knowing when to bring in outside expertise. You will provide independent oversight of Bitvavo's compliance with data protection legislation, with real scope to shape our data strategy.

 - Advise and guide Bitvavo on the policies and standards needed to meet its data protection obligations

 - Engage with data protection authorities, including regular briefings, and maintain accurate records demonstrating GDPR compliance

 - Organise training and awareness activities on data protection and privacy across the company

 - Build a culture that embeds respect for data protection and privacy, acting as the champion for compliance

 - Communicate the privacy implications of new technology and proof of concepts clearly, to both technical and non-technical audiences

 - Assist in addressing mandatory notification and other legal issues in the event of a data loss or breach

 - Challenge the status quo with creative, pragmatic solutions to difficult data protection problems, including on innovative ecommerce and AI projects

 - Devise privacy preserving methods for using large structured, unstructured, transactional and real time data sets, and turn data protection law, statistics and business judgement into actionable recommendations


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

This role requires a qualified lawyer holding a law degree, with at least 7 years of experience in data protection including a minimum of 5 years gained within the EU, which is mandatory given the EU specific nature of this regulation. Experience within the Dutch market of 5 years or more is a strong preference.

 - Proven record of engaging directly with data protection authorities on compliance matters

 - Experience handling data protection and privacy issues for a regulated entity, ideally in tech or ecommerce

 - Strong knowledge of and interest in emerging technologies and their social and economic impact, including customer facing ecommerce

 - Proven ability to analyze complex legal, regulatory and business issues and give sound advice under time pressure

 - Experience managing multiple compliance projects, frameworks or teams, including internal and external resources and delivering training

 - Knowledge of IT security and data analysis methodologies, with experience working alongside IT Security teams in a data driven business

 - A strategic, open minded and user centered thinker, who communicates proactively, connects the dots across industry and regulatory trends, and stays focused on execution

At Bitvavo, we believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation, foster creativity, and lead to better outcomes. We are committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, ability, or any other characteristic. Join us and be part of a team that values and celebrates your unique contributions.

Bitvavo does not accept resumes from staffing, search, or recruitment firms without a signed agreement. If you send us a resume without such an agreement, we may contact the candidate directly without any obligation whatsoever and no fee of any kind will be paid should we hire the candidate.


WHAT WE OFFER

At Bitvavo, we believe in attracting, motivating and retaining talented people through market-competitive offerings that go beyond compensation alone. To learn more about our total rewards package and the benefits we offer, visit our Life at Bitvavo page.

We are looking for a hands-on VP, Product Analytics to lead Product Analytics and build an AI-native analytics operating system across the company’s crypto, stocks, prediction markets, perpetuals, and stock futures products.
You will set the analytics strategy, lead and develop the Product Analytics team, and ensure data consistently shapes product and business decisions. This is a player-coach role: you will operate at executive level while remaining technically close enough to review PRs, guide data modeling and pipeline design, and challenge analytical conclusions.
You will own product and business reporting, experimentation, release measurement, diagnostic analysis, the Amplitude data stack, and the systems through which analytics work is delivered at scale.


Lead Product Analytics
•

Set the vision, priorities, operating model, and quality standards for Product Analytics.

•

Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team.

•

Review analytical and data-engineering PRs, providing guidance on SQL, data models, pipelines, metric definitions, and methodology.

•

Represent Product Analytics in executive and product decision-making.

•

Allocate team capacity toward the company’s highest-impact opportunities.

Build an AI-native analytics operating system
•

Design how analytics work moves from business questions to trusted decisions across intake, data discovery, analysis, validation, reporting, and knowledge management.

•

Build reusable AI tools to automate repetitive workflows, encode analytical standards, and improve the speed, quality, and consistency of delivery.

•

Establish appropriate governance, validation, and human review for high-stakes decisions.

•

Measure the system’s impact on turnaround time, analytical quality, experimentation throughput, and team capacity.

Own product and business reporting
•

Establish trusted KPIs, source-of-truth metrics, dashboards, and executive business reviews.

•

Ensure reporting is accurate, consistent, and focused on decisions—not simply monitoring performance.

•

Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, CRM, Growth, and other functions to align definitions, priorities, and business interpretation.

Build an experimentation culture
•

Make experimentation and evidence core parts of product development.

•

Establish standards for hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, experiment design, causal interpretation, and rollout decisions.

•

Use AI and automation to streamline experiment intake, validation, analysis, and readouts while maintaining analytical rigor.

•

Help product teams move from opinion-led decisions to repeatable test-and-learn practices.

Own analytics platforms and data quality
•

Own the Amplitude data stack, including instrumentation strategy, event taxonomy, governance, data quality, and integration with warehouse reporting.

•

Set standards for product instrumentation and ensure new releases can be measured reliably.

•

Set standards for and review analytical models and pipelines, ensuring metrics remain traceable, reproducible, and trusted as products evolve.

Drive high-impact analysis
•

Lead diagnostic deep-dives into activation, conversion, retention, user behavior, market liquidity, trading execution performance, and product health.

•

Define measurement frameworks and success criteria for major product launches.

•

Oversee post-release evaluations that inform whether the company should iterate, scale, or stop.

•

Identify root causes, challenge weak hypotheses, and translate complex findings into clear recommendations and product actions.

What Success Looks Like: 
•

Leadership operates from trusted, consistent product and business metrics.

•

The Product Analytics team has clear priorities, strong technical standards, and consistently high-quality output.

•

AI-enabled workflows materially improve analytical speed, quality, and capacity.

•

Product teams use experimentation and evidence as standard parts of development.

•

Amplitude instrumentation and taxonomy are reliable, governed, and useful.

•

Major product launches have clear success criteria and rigorous post-release evaluation.

•

High-impact analyses lead to concrete product, operational, and business decisions.

Qualifications: 
•

Proven experience leading Product Analytics teams in a complex, fast-moving organization.

•

Strong hands-on technical judgment, advanced SQL, and experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks.

•

Demonstrated experience using AI to redesign analytics operations—not merely improve individual productivity.

•

Ability to design and implement AI-enabled workflows, reusable agents or tools, validation controls, and analytics knowledge systems.

•

Experience owning a product analytics platform; deep Amplitude experience is strongly preferred.

•

Strong knowledge of experimentation, causal inference, product measurement, and diagnostic analysis.

•

Ability to turn ambiguous business questions into rigorous analysis and clear decisions.

•

Strong product judgment, people leadership, and executive communication skills.

Preferred Experience: 
•

Consumer fintech, trading, marketplaces, or other transaction-heavy products.

•

Exchange mechanics, market liquidity, and experience with multi-asset products.

•

Leading company-wide adoption of new analytics technologies and ways of working.

• Experience of Java in a desktop environment ,Self-organized

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Payward Services is an enterprise infrastructure platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate trading, payments, funding, and digital asset services through a single unified system. It provides coordinated liquidity, custody, compliance, risk management, and settlement capabilities, reducing operational complexity for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers.

Payward's Payments & Blockchain team owns the first and last mile of every dollar that moves in or out of its products. That means dozens of banking partners, PSPs and local rails powering deposits and withdrawals for millions of users.

The team is looking for a product manager to shape the future of this platform, from the architecture underneath to the API layer internal clients build on. At the center is Payward's in-house PSP: a scalable, multi-tenant payments backend with hosted pages, SDKs, embedded components and direct APIs, so any Payward business can plug in and reach pay-in and payout rails worldwide.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the product vision and roadmap for the Payward payments platform, covering both the shared backend and the integration surfaces internal clients build on (hosted pages, SDKs, embedded components and direct APIs)

 - Map requirements across internal clients and use them to evolve the platform's vision and capabilities so it serves a growing range of use cases

 - Partner with engineering to turn the target vision into a sequenced, high-impact roadmap, with milestones every client team can plan against

 - Prioritize across competing client needs, make the trade-offs visible, and say no with a clear rationale

 - Shape the client experience end to end, from first conversation to go-live, so teams can adopt the platform without heavy hand-holding

 - Work with the banking and partnerships teams so each new PSP or bank integration is built once on the platform and reaches every Payward business

 - Bring compliance, risk and legal requirements across Payward's entities and jurisdictions into the roadmap early, before they become launch blockers

 - Set and track platform success metrics, such as time to launch a rail for an existing client, time for a new client to go live, share of rails available through the platform, and payment success rates

 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years of product management experience, ideally in a platform, API or infrastructure role where your customers were other internal teams or developers

 - Working knowledge of payments: pay-ins and payouts, PSPs and acquirers, bank rails (ACH, SEPA, Faster Payments, SWIFT and local methods), and how money flows between them

 - Strong technical fluency. You can read an RFC, challenge an architecture decision, and write an API spec that engineers respect

 - Experience shipping developer-facing products such as APIs, SDKs, or embeddable UI components

 - Clear, structured writing. You turn complex system designs into docs that product, compliance and business stakeholders can all act on

 - Skill at managing many stakeholders with different priorities, and building alignment without direct authority

 - Comfort working with data to set goals and measure platform adoption and performance

 
 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience at a PSP, payment orchestrator or payments infrastructure company, or building one in-house

 - Background with multi-tenant SaaS or B2B2C platforms

 - Familiarity with crypto, stablecoins or on/off-ramps

 - Experience working across multiple regulated legal entities or licensing regimes

 
 
 



Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

About the Team

The Compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance program and culture of the company. We’re a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company’s regulatory obligations and enterprise risk.

About the Opportunity

The successful candidate will have prior transaction monitoring/investigations experience in the financial services, FinTech or cryptocurrency industries. You will help support the Special Investigations team, focusing on analyzing blockchain data to identify potential illicit activities, money laundering and terrorist financing, involving cryptocurrencies. The job requires a mix of technical expertise, investigative skills, and knowledge of crypto markets and blockchain technology.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Conduct in-depth investigations of complex AML cases, ensuring thorough analysis and adherence to regulatory requirements, through investigation of blockchain transactions to track and identify suspicious or illicit activities such as money laundering, and other criminal activities.

•

Analyze data to identify process gaps and opportunities, and partner with Compliance, Training and other FIU stakeholders to recommend mitigating activities for risk and close process gaps.

Evaluate AML transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting requirements for all countries where applicable.

•

Collaborate with external partners, including financial institutions, government agencies, and blockchain companies, to share intelligence and insights. Work closely with law enforcement agencies, regulators, and legal teams to provide insights and evidence for criminal investigations.

•

Stay abreast of changes to the cryptocurrency industry, financial crime trends, and regulatory requirements to assess impact to Transaction Monitoring.

•

Support team training and knowledge sharing, fostering a collaborative environment focused on ongoing learning and professional growth.

•

3-5 years of direct and strong technical experience in BSA/AML investigations and operations in relevant financial crimes, transaction monitoring and investigation roles.

Demonstrated knowledge of BSA/AML, KYC regulations, risks and controls implementation globally.

•

Strong understanding of blockchain technology, cryptocurrency protocols, and decentralized networks.

•

Experience performing in a fast-paced environment and proven ability to meet deadlines.

•

Self-motivated, critical thinker and adept at working independently and in a dispersed team environment covering multiple and varied tasks.

Intuitive, highly ethical, and comfortable to question and challenge the status quo.

•

Strong communication and presentation skills, both verbal and written. Proficiency in writing detailed investigative reports and communicating complex technical findings to non-technical stakeholders.

•

Experience working independently and with team members of all levels.

Nice to Haves

•

Prior experience working in a multi-national or matrix environment.

•

Familiarity with commonly used transaction monitoring & reporting tool(s), such as Solidus Labs, Chainalysis, or Elliptic.

•

Relevant certifications in blockchain technology, digital forensics, or financial crime investigations such as CAMS, CFCS are a plus.

Competitive total compensation package

•

L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development

Various team building programs and company events

Wellness and meal allowances

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependents

More that we love to tell you along the process!

Brand Voice & Editorial Standards

Platform migrations, retiring shared dependencies, standardising how every squad works and rolling out new engineering practices all cut across those boundaries, and you will be the person who holds that work end to end.
You will run cross-team technical programs, help drive and improve the engineering processes everyone relies on, and make sure both are backed by real data rather than assumptions. This is not a people management role, and you will not write production code. You do need to be technical enough that engineers treat you as a peer. The role is broad and hands-on. In a typical week you might sequence a Kafka topic migration across four squads, fix a company-wide process that keeps stalling at the same step, pull numbers from a database to settle a question about impact, and ship a small automation that removes a recurring manual task for the whole department. Continuous improvement and AI are central to the role: you will constantly look for better ways for engineering to work and apply AI where it clearly improves throughput, quality or speed.

• Run cross-team technical programs such as platform migrations, dependency removals, standardisation initiatives, decommissioning, and large infrastructure changes. For each one, break broad goals into sequenced plans with named owners.

• Query data directly using SQL, dashboards, and APIs, and reconcile what Jira reports with what systems actually show.

• Identify recurring manual work across engineering and automate it, using AI where it adds real value, then measure whether the automation delivered actual savings.

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Marketing

The Prediction Markets Operations team turns real-world events into clearly defined event contracts. We support markets across their full lifecycle—from an initial idea, through configuration and launch, into live operations, and finally to accurate resolution. Our work sits at the intersection of current events, marketplaces, and regulated products, and it demands precision at every step.

The team is responsible for making sure every contract is: clearly and objectively written, based on reliable, authoritative resolution sources, accurately configured, supported with appropriate images and content, thoroughly reviewed before launch, monitored while live, and resolved accurately and consistently.

The Role: Prediction Markets Operations Intern

This is a detail-oriented, hands-on internship for someone interested in marketplaces, operations, current events, financial technology, or regulated products. You will perform time-sensitive operational work and learn firsthand how prediction markets move from an idea to a live and, ultimately, settled contract.

Success in this role depends on accuracy, sound judgment, reliability, and operational discipline. Just as important is the willingness to escalate uncertainty rather than guess. You will support, coordinate, research, prepare, review, and execute work under established procedures, working closely with partners across Prediction Markets, Operations, Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, Design, Marketing, and our liquidity partners.

This will be a semester long internship program with 3 days a week in person at our New York City, NY office from January to April 2027.

Responsibilities:

Contract Research and Market Listings

• Research potential prediction-market contract ideas.

• Help turn ideas into precise, objective binary questions.

• Identify reliable and authoritative public resolution sources.

• Flag ambiguity, potentially prohibited subject matter, or questions requiring Compliance or Legal review.

• Prepare contract specifications, including outcomes, dates, descriptions, tickers, resolution criteria, and other listing details.

• Create and configure event contracts in the Contract Management System, or assist with structured CSV uploads, under established procedures.

• Support research and documentation related to product requirements and filings.

Quality Assurance and Launch Operations

• Perform pre-launch and post-upload quality assurance.

• Verify contract names, outcomes, ordering, start times, expiration times, resolution criteria, and designated sources.

• Review dates and times carefully, including UTC-based fields.

• Compare contracts with relevant external prediction markets when appropriate, and identify unintended differences in outcomes, timing, or mechanics.

• Confirm that event and social images are present and appropriate.

• Upload or update approved event images, social images, and display settings.

• Coordinate launch information with internal stakeholders and liquidity partners.

• Identify discrepancies and escalate issues before launch.

Customer and Live-Market Support

• Review, triage, and investigate prediction-market support tickets.

• Gather relevant facts, document findings, and route issues appropriately.

• Monitor live markets for incorrect content, timing discrepancies, operational issues, or unexpected behavior.

• Follow established incident-escalation procedures when urgent technical or operational issues arise.

• Maintain accurate trackers, checklists, SOPs, and internal documentation.

• Identify opportunities to improve repetitive workflows and reduce manual work.

Market Monitoring and Resolution

• Monitor contracts approaching expiration or awaiting resolution.

• Research outcomes using the contract’s designated resolution source.

• Prepare a proposed outcome, source links, and a concise rationale for internal review.

• Double-check resolution information against authoritative sources.

• Escalate unclear, conflicting, delayed, or incomplete source information rather than guessing.

• Execute approved market settlements in the Contract Management System after required training, review, and approval.

• Settlement activity is performed only under established procedures, supervision, access controls, and approval requirements. Accuracy is critical, because completed settlements may not be reversible.

• Document completed resolutions according to team procedures.

Scheduled Monitoring Coverage

• Participate in a scheduled rotation for brief evening or weekend monitoring.

• This is lightweight, scheduled coverage—not continuous or unrestricted on-call work.

• Interns will primarily identify and escalate issues to the appropriate full-time team.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Associate’s, or Master’s degree.

• Exceptional attention to detail.

• Strong written communication.

• Ability to research information and distinguish authoritative sources from unreliable ones.

• Sound judgment and a willingness to escalate uncertainty.

• Comfort with detailed, repeatable, process-driven tasks.

• Ability to manage time-sensitive work without sacrificing accuracy.

• Dependability and follow-through.

• Basic proficiency with spreadsheets and web-based business tools.

• Ability to work in-office.

• Availability for the scheduled, lightweight evening or weekend monitoring rotation.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Internship, academic, or project experience in operations, customer support, research, quality assurance, content operations, marketplaces, fintech, or another detail-oriented environment.

• Familiarity with prediction markets, financial markets, sports, politics, economics, or major current events.

• Experience with ticketing platforms, content-management systems, administrative tools, dashboards, or structured data entry.

• Interest in regulated products or operational risk.

• Experience creating or maintaining process documentation.

• Comfort learning unfamiliar internal tools quick.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Job Description
Data Privacy Manager

About IG Group

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here.

About the Role

IG's Data & AI team is scaling up how the business governs, understands, and trusts its data. As our Data Privacy Manager, you'll be the Group's central point of contact for data privacy - closing the gap between policy and practice, taking ownership of the RoPA process, DPIAs, DSAR protocol, retention practices, and breach reporting, and giving IG a single accountable home for data privacy compliance.

About the Team

This role sits within the Data & AI team, reporting into the Head of Data Governance & Strategy. This is an individual contributor role and the first hire into a newly centralised function, so it requires someone comfortable working on their own initiative and building relationships with stakeholders at all levels. As the function scales, this role will pick up direct reports.

Key Responsibilities

As Data Privacy Manager, you'll lead the strategic and day-to-day agenda for data privacy at IG, partnering closely with Legal, Risk, Compliance, HR, Procurement, Technology, and Product colleagues. You'll help evolve a privacy capability that is rigorous where it needs to be and practical everywhere it can be.

• Be the central point of contact for data privacy - act as the go-to for all data privacy related questions across the Group, from policy interpretation to practical guidance for staff at all levels.
• Support the governance framework - support the development of the data privacy governance framework, from DPIAs and privacy by design to retention, RoPA and third-party diligence.
• Own cross-border data transfers - put in place and maintain the mechanisms that allow personal data to move lawfully between IG's UK, EU and international entities, such as Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement, and adequacy assessments.
• Own the regulatory interface - manage breach notifications to the relevant regulator within the required regulatory timeframe, DPIA consultations, and centralised data privacy reporting to SLT/Board.
• Advise on privacy by design - advise product and business teams on the privacy implications of new products, changes and customer journeys.
• Translate law into practical guidance - translate UK privacy law into clear, proportionate recommendations that enable responsible decisions.
• Manage complex privacy incidents - including regulatory notification and engagement with affected individuals where required.
• Strengthen privacy awareness - across the business and help build out the privacy function as it grows - running training programmes that go beyond policy awareness to cover breach recognition and escalation for all staff.
• Contribute to the Group's approach to data risk - across a broad range of business activity.

Role Requirements

• 5+ years' experience - in a dedicated data privacy role within a regulated environment.
• Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and EU GDPR - together with practical awareness of other privacy regimes relevant to IG's international footprint, including practical experience running DPIAs, RoPA and DSAR processes end-to-end.
• Experience operating within a multi-jurisdictional group structure - (e.g. UK, EU, APAC).
• Experience designing and embedding privacy governance documentation - policies, procedures, and escalation routes, ideally in an organisation without an existing dedicated function.
• Comfortable acting as the primary point of contact - for regulators, and for internal Audit and Risk stakeholders, on data privacy matters.
• Strong communication skills - able to translate legal and regulatory requirements into practical guidance for Product, Technology, HR, and other business teams.
• Experience delivering data privacy training and awareness programmes.

Desirable
• Experience in UK financial services or a similarly regulated industry.
• Practical exposure to AI/ML-related privacy considerations - (e.g. automated decision-making, Article 22).
• Professional certification in data protection/privacy - (e.g. CIPP/E, CIPM, BCS Certificate in Data Protection).

The Perks

It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.

• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Derivatives and Trading products sit in one of the most heavily regulated and fastest-moving parts of Payward's regulatory perimeter, and the estate is still expanding across a US venue and clearing stack, a UK venue, EEA distribution and a Bermuda entity. Today that work is owned in fragments. This is a net-new, function-owning role created to put global derivatives structuring strategy to a single senior owner. This DGC will be responsible for the global suite of derivatives products as well as Payward’s trading products.

Products. Futures and options across the group, and margin in the US, and a set of trading products, including but not limited to leveraged and liquidity products, prediction markets, indices and market data, evaluation-based trading services and structured yield. The DGC will help define the delineation of these products between the new function and the existing Product Legal team.

Entities and regulators. A US venue and clearing stack (FCM/NFA, DCM, DCO), a UK FCA-authorised derivatives venue, EEA derivatives distribution under CySEC permissions, and a Bermuda DABA entity serving the rest of world and others. The general counsel of our acquired US futures brokerage (NinjaTrader) reports into this function.

Team. Senior derivatives and trading counsel across the US, UK and EEA, with the function set to grow, and the general counsel of the acquired US futures brokerage.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own global derivatives structuring strategy — product structure, venue and entity architecture, clearing models, and how a single coherent derivatives offering is delivered to clients across several separately licensed entities.

 - Together with Payward’s Regulatory Legal team, solve the cross-entity problems that sit in no single product — hub-and-spoke architecture, unified balances, cross-margining, and where risk and client relationships actually sit across the group. These are the hardest questions we answer.

 - Be the named senior legal owner for the derivatives and trading product lines, wired into the product launch process from the start rather than consulted at the end, and the single senior route into Legal for derivatives and trading.

 - Lead and build the team — hire, level and develop senior derivatives counsel across jurisdictions, and build depth and succession into a function that is currently thin at the top.

 - Partner with Global Policy and Government Relations as the senior legal counterpart for derivatives regulatory engagement with the CFTC, NFA, FCA, BMA, CySEC and others, pre-socialising positions with regulators and internal leadership before they land, not after.

 - Support the supervised estates that carry derivatives permissions, working with Regulatory Legal on continuous supervisory relationships and on new permissions and variations tied to product launches.

 - Bring structuring judgement in-house, and direct external counsel where genuinely specialist input is required.

 - Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Attorney admitted to practice in the US, or qualified lawyer (Solicitor/Barrister of England & Wales, Irish Solicitor/Barrister, or equivalent admitted in an EU Member State).

 - 18+ years’ post-qualification experience (PQE) in financial services regulatory law gained at a regulated financial services institution, major liquidity provider or in a law firm/private practice supporting such clients, with demonstrated ability to independently own BAU regulatory workstreams.

 - Experience supporting regulator engagement (e.g., with the CFTC, NFA, FCA, Cysec, or an equivalent EU competent authority), including notifications, information requests, and supervisory correspondence.

 - Substantial senior in-house or equivalent experience in derivatives legal, with demonstrated ownership of structuring strategy rather than transactional execution alone.

 - Deep, expert-level command of at least one of the following derivatives regulatory regimes — US (CFTC, NFA; FCM, DCM and DCO structures), UK (FCA), EEA, or an offshore regime (e.g., Bermuda) — together with a high degree of fluency in at least one other. No single regime is treated as the required one; what matters is genuine mastery of one and strong working command of a second.

 - Direct experience with virtual asset markets. This combination is scarce and it is the core of the role.

 - Experience structuring a product offering across multiple licensed entities in different jurisdictions, and holding a view on where activity, risk and the client relationship should sit.

 - A track record of building or materially scaling a legal function or team, including hiring, levelling and succession.

 - The range to operate at function level, setting strategy for the function as a whole, organising it to stay ahead of the regulatory perimeter, and holding senior lawyers to account for results and behaviour, not only for output.

 - Credibility with regulators and the judgement to take positions in front of them.

 - Comfort operating as the senior legal voice in a fast-moving, product-led business where the regulatory perimeter changes underneath you, and comfort staying close to the work rather than managing at a distance.

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Exposure to prediction markets, margin lending, or tokenized and structured products.

 - Experience integrating acquired regulated entities, and their legal teams, into a group legal function.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About The Opportunity

OKX is building out its equities and tokenized securities business. This is a post-trade and brokerage systems product role — you will own the layer that sits between our users and the securities markets: order management, execution, settlement, asset servicing and reconciliation.

We have strong crypto product and engineering talent. What this role brings is depth in brokerage architecture and securities market structure: how these systems are built, why they are built that way, and what breaks at scale. You will be the internal authority on that, and your judgment will shape decisions that are expensive to reverse.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Own the brokerage core — order management, execution and routing, instrument lifecycle and trading status, settlement and reconciliation.

•

Shape account, custody and clearing architecture, along with the operating model required to run it.

•

Own corporate actions and asset servicing end to end, in both conventional and on-chain form.

•

Define how securities risk and margin frameworks coexist with those of a 24/7 digital asset market.

•

Bring market structure, execution quality and regulatory requirements into product decisions early, before they become blockers.

•

Set the standard for rigour — write PRDs precise enough to build from, and lead alignment across engineering, risk, legal, compliance and treasury.

What We Look For In You

Domain Depth

•

5+ years in post-trade or brokerage systems product management. We strongly prefer candidates from internet and licensed brokerages — Futu, Tiger, Interactive Brokers, Robinhood, Webull, Longbridge — as well as clearing firms and brokerage infrastructure providers.

•

Architectural perspective. You have a clear view of where responsibility belongs across the order, execution, clearing, settlement, asset servicing and ledger layers, and of what goes wrong downstream when a boundary is drawn in the wrong place.

•

Depth across the order and execution path. Order types and parameters, state machine design, idempotency across an external execution boundary, cancel/replace and partial-fill semantics, timeout and exception recovery. This is the core craft of the role.

•

End-to-end ownership of at least one area beyond the order path — clearing and settlement, corporate actions and asset servicing, margin and risk, securities lending, or position and cash reconciliation.

•

Commercial and historical perspective. You understand how a brokerage actually earns, how each revenue line constrains the systems beneath it, and why the industry made the structural choices it did.

Ways of Working

•

Strong technical intuition. You are comfortable discussing system architecture and data flows with engineers. You do not need to be a developer, but you think with the rigour of one.

•

You design for the exceptions — the halted symbol, the timed-out counterparty, the partial fill, the corporate action mid-flight — not just the order that goes through.

•

You run programs, not just write specs. You produce rigorous PRDs independently, drive alignment across engineering, risk, legal, compliance and treasury, and own the full lifecycle from requirements through post-launch review.

•

You write precisely, and can make complex mechanics legible to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

•

High agency. You are comfortable taking an open question all the way to a shipped, reconciled system, and making calls with incomplete information.

•

Proficiency in Mandarin is required to communicate effectively with internal engineering and product stakeholders in the China-based R&D center.

Nice-To-Haves

•

Product experience with margin financing or securities lending.

•

Exposure to tokenized securities, digital asset custody, or on-chain settlement.

•

Experience integrating with broker-dealer or clearing APIs, as either the integrator or the provider.

•

Hands-on experience with multi-jurisdiction regulatory frameworks — SEC/FINRA, MiFID II, or equivalent.

•

A track record of launching a brokerage product in a new market from zero.

•

Fluency in English to support communication with global product and business stakeholders.

•

Genuine curiosity about what happens when securities markets meet 24/7 markets.

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

• L&D programs and education subsidy for employees' growth and development

•

Various team building programs and company events

• Wellness and meal allowances

• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

• More that we love to tell you along the process!

Please note that Hong Kong is a group-level service hub, and OKX does not carry on a business of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong.

We are seeking a highly motivated Technology and Security Risk Manager within the Second Line of Defence (2LOD). You will be responsible for continuously refining and scaling the Technology and Security oversight program, guiding first-line of defence (1LOD) execution, and providing independent risk challenge.

You will be a key member of OKX's Risk team, helping to shape and scale the firm’s 2LOD Security & Data Risk programs. You’ll work closely with stakeholders including Engineering, Product, Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit.

You will play a key role in developing and implementing a comprehensive Technology and Security Risk Management program. This includes 2LOD oversight of technology defects, issues, and incidents, Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA), key risk indicators (KRIs) and reporting.

The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of Technology Risk (including Technology Resilience, Change Management, SDLC, CI/CD pipeline, and software quality assurance) and Cybersecurity (covering internal and external threat vectors, control weaknesses, and organisational cyber hygiene). We are looking for a candidate with a strong drive for improvement and career growth.

What You’ll Be Doing

Collaborate with internal stakeholders across the company to proactively identify, escalate, assess, and mitigate Technology and Security risks, ensuring adherence to the Technology Risk Policy.

Providing oversight of Technology and Security Risk incidents and issues, and partnering with 1LOD stakeholders to enhance related processes and ensure effective oversight

Lead the Technology Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) process from a 2LOD perspective, ensuring adherence to the ERM RCSA methodology, and providing effective challenge and oversight of 1LOD Security risks and controls.

Support the Security Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) definition, monitoring, and reporting.

Supporting the implementation and ongoing enhancement of Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) systems to enable effective risk oversight

Advocate and support the implementation of Risk Management frameworks for technology stakeholders, serving as a trusted advisor for the first line.

Stay up to date on emerging trends and regulations in the digital asset space, proactively identifying and addressing new risk considerations.

What We Look For In You

•

8+ years in information security, with a strong security architecture or technical security background; fintech, crypto or cloud-native experience preferred.

•

Practical experience designing, implementing or reviewing cloud, IAM, cryptographic, network or application security controls.

•

Experience in risk oversight, or readiness to transition, with the technical judgement to challenge controls and recommend proportionate improvements.

•

Ability to threat-model systems and assess technical evidence, including architecture diagrams, IAM policies, logging configurations and dependencies.

•

Working knowledge of cloud resilience, multi-region/AZ failover, RTO/RPO and disaster recovery testing.

•

Familiarity with NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2 and relevant privacy requirements, including GDPR and PDPA, and their application to technical controls.

•

Ability to independently assess and test controls, evaluate incidents and drive remediation with engineering and security teams; GRC platform experience desirable.

•

Clear written and verbal communication, translating technical findings into prioritised actions for business stakeholders and governance committees.

•

Strong stakeholder management skills, providing constructive challenge and collaborating across functions and geographies.

•

A proactive, adaptable approach, with confidence taking ownership and improving practices in a fast-paced environment.

•

A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience; CISSP, CCSP, cloud security/architecture, CISA or CISM qualifications desirable.

Copenhagen, Denmark

About the job

At Saxo, technology is our business. Every trade, every client interaction, every product launch and every market opportunity rely on a complex technology landscape operating securely, reliably and at scale. That's where you come in.

We're looking for an IT Audit Manager who is curious, challenging and passionate about understanding how technology really works. Someone who enjoys asking the questions others don't, uncovering hidden risks, and helping strengthen the controls that keep a global financial institution running. That’s what we are looking for our work in Group Internal Audit (GIA).

As Group Internal Audit, we report directly to the Board of Directors and provides independent assurance on the risks that matter most to Saxo.

This is not your typical audit role!

You'll have a front-row seat to the technologies, processes, and risks that matter most to Saxo. From cloud platforms and cybersecurity to software delivery and operational resilience, you'll assess whether the foundations of our technology environment are strong enough to support a growing global business.

Many of the IT audits we perform in GIA are General IT Controls such as Access management, IT operations, Physical Security, Change management, Backup and Recovery.
These controls may not always make the headlines, but they are often the difference between a secure, resilient organisation and one exposed to significant operational, financial or regulatory risk.

If you enjoy understanding how infrastructure and systems are built, controlled, and governed, you'll feel right at home with GIA.

Responsibilities

• Leading high-impact IT audits across Saxo's global technology landscape.
• Assessing the effectiveness of General IT Controls, a key focus area of our audit portfolio.
• Evaluating whether critical systems are properly secured, administered, changed and monitored.
• Challenging the status quo and identifying opportunities to strengthen controls and reduce risk.
• Engaging with engineers, architects, security specialists, technology leaders and executives.
• Translating technical findings into clear business insights and practical recommendations.
• Contributing to audits covering cybersecurity, cloud services, resilience, third-party risk, data management, and emerging technologies such as AI.

Your profile

You may be an experienced IT auditor, IT risk professional, technology consultant or security specialist looking to move into another role.

You'll likely bring:

• Strong knowledge of General IT Controls (GITCs) and technology risk management.
• Experience assessing areas such as user access management, change management, IT operations and cybersecurity.
• The ability to understand complex technology environments and explain risks in a simple, business-focused way.
• Confidence to engage constructively with stakeholders at all levels.
• A curious mindset and a desire to continuously learn.

Professional certifications such as CISA, CIA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP or equivalent is an advantage.

Join us if you want to:

• Understand how a digital bank really works behind the scenes.
• Be recognised as a trusted advisor on technology risk and controls.
• Work on audits that go beyond compliance and drive real improvement.
• Help strengthen the General IT Controls that form the backbone of a secure and resilient organisation.

Technology moves fast. Controls need to keep up. Help us make sure they do.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.
When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

Job TitleSenior HRBP (Tech, Product + Ops)

Job Description
Who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.

A word about our People team
Thanks to recent changes to our business units, we’ve gone back to first principles with our partnering function. Our business partners partner: that is their craft and their whole job. The deep specialist work in Reward, Talent, Learning and Development, and Employee Relations sits with our Centre of Excellence, and partners draw on that expertise rather than trying to do all of it themselves.

What that gives you is a role with focus. You get to know a part of the business properly, build relationships that mean something, and spend your time on the work that actually shifts performance. It also means you are never on your own, because you have specialists behind you.
This is the senior step on our partnering ladder for Tech, Product and Ops. You will hold the largest and most senior client group in the area, and you will lead a small team of two HR Business Partners, based in Kraków and Bangalore, who partner the layers of the business below you. You will be judged on the quality of your own partnering as much as on the strength and consistency of the team you lead.

Who will you partner with?
Functions or business areas: Product, Technology and Operations for IG Consumer
Leadership team you support: The Chief Product Officer, the CTO - IG Consumer and the Operations Director, and their leadership teams
Approximate population: c. 500, across three layers of the team
Locations covered: London (base), with population across the UK, Kraków (Poland) and Bangalore (India)

What is the role?
You will be the senior People partner to the leadership team above. This is a role for someone who has done the fundamentals of partnering well and is ready for the harder, more ambiguous work: the restructure that hasn’t started yet, the senior case that needs careful handling, the leadership team that is not yet performing as a team.

You will be close to the most senior leaders in your area and you will need to be genuinely useful to them. That means understanding the commercial picture, having a view, and being willing to hold your position when it would be easier not to. It also means being the person who makes things happen, not just the person who advises.

What will you do?
Partner senior leaders
• Be the trusted People partner to your leadership team, in the room for the decisions that matter rather than told about them afterwards.
• Coach senior leaders on their own leadership, their team dynamics and the calls they find hardest. Challenge them well.
• Hold a position under pressure. Balance what the business wants with what is right for IG and for our people, and be respected for how you do it.
• Manage competing priorities across several senior stakeholders without losing pace or losing anyone’s trust.
• Lead, coach and develop your two HR Business Partners in Kraków and Bangalore, setting the standard for partnering across all three layers of the team and ensuring consistent quality wherever colleagues sit.

Lead organisation design and change
• Lead restructures and reorganisations in your area from first conversation to final implementation, compliantly and with care for the people affected.
• Advise leaders on operating model, structure, spans, layers, levels and job design before decisions are made, so structure follows strategy rather than personalities.
• Build the case for change, including the numbers, and take leaders and colleagues with you through it.

Own the hardest employee relations work
• Take the most sensitive and complex cases in your area, including senior level and cross border matters, working closely with our Employee Relations specialists and Legal.
• Be accountable for the quality and consistency of ER practice across your area, and for making sure risk is surfaced early.
• Use what you see across cases to fix causes. Feed the patterns back so policy and manager capability improve.

Set the bar on culture and performance
• Own the engagement and culture agenda for a large or complex population, and hold leaders accountable for their own scores rather than carrying it for them.
• Set the standard for what good performance management looks like in your area. Push leaders to differentiate properly, recognise the best and act on the rest.
• Make sure your area’s strongest people are known, developed and kept, and that succession risk in critical roles is understood.

Make the wider People function better
• Shape how group and divisional programmes land across more than your own patch, and feed what you see on the ground back into the Centre of Excellence so that what they design works.
• Raise the bar in the team through mentoring, role modelling and improving how we partner. Be someone the more junior partners learn from, without needing a management title to do it.
• Work well across our locations, and help the team understand where local context should change our approach.

Bring insight, not just information
• Use people, cost and commercial data to bring your leaders insight they had not asked for.
• Build and defend a business case, in the language the business uses.
• Watch the external market and regulatory picture so you can see what is coming rather than react to it.

What does success look like?
• Your leadership team trusts you and involves you early.
• Change in your area is delivered on time, compliantly, and with colleagues understanding why.
• The hardest cases are handled well and quietly, and nothing significant surprises us.
• Engagement and performance in your area improve, and leaders are empowered to own that improvement themselves.
• Managers and more junior partners around you are visibly better because you are there.

What will you need?
• Significant HR business partnering experience, including partnering leaders at or close to executive level.
• Experience supporting Product + Tech teams, familiarity with relevant methodologies, ceremonies and what good looks like.
• A clear track record leading organisational change and design.
• Deep employee relations capability and the judgement to handle senior, sensitive and cross-border cases (with support).
• Strong employment law knowledge for at least one of the markets we operate in, and the appetite to get up to speed on the others.
• Commercial credibility. You can hold your own in a business conversation and connect people decisions to cost, risk and delivery.
• The confidence to challenge senior leaders constructively and to hold a position when it matters.
• Experience coaching or developing others; prior line management experience is an advantage given this role leads two HR Business Partners.
• Experience working across locations and cultures, or a clear ability to do it well.

Helpful but not essential: experience in financial services, fintech or another regulated industry, and experience working in a matrix model alongside a Centre of Excellence.

One more thing
We believe diversity is vital to our success. It fuels creativity, drives innovation and sets us up to win globally. We are committed to building teams with a range of perspectives and skills, so we encourage applications from people with all kinds of backgrounds and experiences. If you need any adjustments to the process, just tell us and we will sort it.

The Perks
